findings.summary: The caption opens with a bare series label instead of a hook, burying the actual hook in the second sentence.
findings.evidence: First sentence: "Part 2 of BINARY SEARCH PATTERNS." The hook — "Binary search is not one problem, it is eight patterns wearing the same loop." — is only the second sentence, past the feed truncation point.
findings.fix: Lead with the hook and demote the part label: "Binary search is not one problem — it is eight patterns wearing the same loop. Part 2 of BINARY SEARCH PATTERNS. Seven handwritten pages take you from the overflow-safe mid formula to bounds, search-on-answer, rotated arrays, peaks, infinite arrays and 2D matrices, then close with a one-page interview cheat sheet. Save this one before your next coding round."
Run the fit pass — it adds material from the book without removing anything.

findings.summary: The three-panel pointer visual is split across two pages, leaving the "FOUND" panel orphaned on page 3 between two callouts and the decision flowchart.
findings.evidence: Page 2 carries the panels captioned "Target in LEFT half -> high = mid - 1" and "Target in RIGHT half -> low = mid + 1"; the third, "Target FOUND at mid, arr[mid] = 8", appears on page 3 after the "Loop-shape trap" and "Key Takeaways" callouts.
findings.fix: Move the "Target FOUND at mid" array diagram to page 2 so all three panels sit together in LEFT / RIGHT / FOUND order, matching the three-case comparison the code template above them teaches.

findings.summary: The "Key Takeaways" closing callout is placed second on the final page, ahead of two teaching blocks that still introduce new material.
findings.evidence: Page 3 block order is: "Loop-shape trap" callout, "Key Takeaways" callout ("Binary Search is a ==family of patterns==, not one problem..."), the "Target FOUND at mid" array diagram, then the "Binary Search Decision Flow" flowchart.
findings.fix: Move the "Key Takeaways" callout to the end of page 3, after the decision flowchart, so the summary closes the part instead of interrupting it.

findings.summary: The caption says binary search is "eight patterns" while page 1 enumerates fifteen numbered patterns in the card grid.
findings.evidence: caption: "it is eight patterns wearing the same loop" vs page 1 cards numbered "1 Iterative binary search" … "15 Infinite sorted array"
findings.fix: Change the caption to match the enumeration — e.g. "it is fifteen patterns wearing the same loop" — or say "eight complexity profiles" if the intent was the eight-row complexity table on page 2.

findings.summary: The overflow pitfall names the broken mid formula but withholds the correct one until the next page, so page 1 depends on page 2 to be actionable.
findings.evidence: Page 1: "Wrong mid: `(low + high) / 2` can **overflow**" — the safe form appears only on page 2, in the code note "overflow-safe mid, sorted input only" and the bullet "Huge indices: use `lo + (hi - lo) / 2`".
findings.fix: Rewrite the page 1 bullet to carry the correction inline, e.g. "Wrong mid: `(low + high) / 2` can **overflow** — use `low + (high - low) / 2`".

findings.summary: The "Binary Search Decision Flow" flowchart has no edge returning to the loop and puts the "Condition found?" test after a half has already been discarded, so it depicts a single non-iterating pass rather than binary search.
findings.evidence: edges: {"from":"left","to":"found"},{"from":"right","to":"found"},{"from":"found","to":"ret","label":"yes"},{"from":"found","to":"nf","label":"no / best ans"} — no edge from left/right/found back to "loop", and the "cond" diamond emits only "too big"/"too small" with no equal/found branch, unlike the page-2 template `if (a[mid] == t) return mid;`
findings.fix: Move the found test to directly after `mid` (cond: equal → ret; too big → LEFT; too small → RIGHT) and add back edges {"from":"left","to":"loop"} and {"from":"right","to":"loop"}, with the loop's exit edge going to "nf" (labelled "low > high").

findings.summary: The decision flowchart puts the "Condition found?" check after the low/high update, contradicting the template code on page 2 where a match returns before any shrink.
findings.evidence: Flowchart edges run "cond" -> "left"/"right" -> "found" ("Condition found?"), while the page 2 code reads "if (a[mid] == t) return mid;" before "if (a[mid] < t) lo = mid + 1; else hi = mid - 1;".
findings.fix: Reorder the flowchart so "Check condition" branches to a found/return path directly, with the LEFT / RIGHT updates on the not-found branch looping back to "while (low <= high)", and add the loop-back edge that is currently missing.

findings.summary: The loop-shape trap asserts that `high = mid - 1` under `while (low < high)` can skip the answer, with no example showing the skip.
findings.evidence: "With `while (low < high)` never write `high = mid - 1` — you can step **over** the answer."
findings.fix: Add a two-line concrete case to the callout (e.g. lower bound on arr = [1,3,3,5], target = 3: with `high = mid - 1` low overshoots index 1) so the reader can see the failure rather than take it on assertion.
